claims.head: Toronto gives up shots, and Colorado takes them
claims.body: Few teams shoot as often as Colorado: 70.2 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5, 1st in the league. Toronto sits 28th of 32 at keeping shots down.

claims.head: Colorado feeds on loose pucks
claims.body: Colorado turns takeaways into chances as well as almost anyone (4th of 32: 7.7% of its chances come right after winning the puck). Toronto ranks 23rd at avoiding breakdowns.

claims.head: Expect a track meet
claims.body: Toronto’s games average 84.5 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined (4th of 32 for pace); Colorado’s average 89.0 (1st).

notes.text: O. Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 5 games, up from 6% last season.

COL.head: A big edge for Colorado
COL.body: Colorado has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Anything short of a win would be a surprise, though Toronto can make a game of it if it pounces on loose pucks.

TOR.head: A steep climb for Toronto
TOR.body: Colorado has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Toronto could still pull it off if it pounces on loose pucks, but it might need a miracle.
